quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Research shows that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Often confusing to other drivers.
Less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on during the day is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: To check tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Look at the tire and estimate the pressure.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire that is not fully inflated may still look okay, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
Any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have loose or frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
Leather gloves.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only if you will carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a complete pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should take only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body usually removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use one brake, never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together to stop. The brakes work best when used at the same time.

questions.question: What helps drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Ride with your headlight on.
Swerve within your lane to get attention.
Raise your arms.
Avoid using your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, use your headlight and position yourself in the lane where oncoming drivers can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If someone drank eight alcoholic drinks four hours ago, about how many drinks likely remain in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see clearly to the sides.
It limits your side vision.
It is usually uncomfortable.
It has no labels or markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the maker's name, instructions, and safety standard information.

questions.question: Which fabric protects motorcycle riders best?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Wool
Polyester

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants give the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual
A general book about motorcycles
Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing someone else's motorcycle.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink:

options.text: It can affect your judgment and riding ability.
It has no effect on your body.
It affects your body for only a short time.
Coffee can remove the effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your judgment and riding ability.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding skills. Your body needs time to remove alcohol. Coffee cannot speed this up.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Try not to be noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Signal your turns and lane changes, use your brake light, and stay in proper lane position. Keep safe distance from other vehicles and watch ahead for hazards.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If the drive chain or belt fails, your rear wheel will suddenly lose power.

questions.question: You have been drinking. If you wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still feel side effects.
You are okay if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still feel side effects.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's alcohol per hour. But alcohol can build up in your system even at this pace. Your judgment and ability can still be impaired.

questions.question: What should you do if someone tailgates you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes when safe and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:

options.text: Engine braking
Acceleration
Upshifting
Coasting

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking
questions.explanation: Downshifting to a lower gear works like braking. That is why it is called engine braking.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It should be done to help riders practice different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of your lane.
Always stay on the far left side of your lane.
Slowly zigzag back and forth across the grating.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may make your motorcycle weave slightly. This is not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weave is dangerous and can pull you out of your lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into small gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slower, start braking earlier, increase your following distance, and wait for larger gaps when entering or merging into traffic.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good quality helmet that is fastened securely.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good quality helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good quality helmet that is fastened securely is the single most effective thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Where should a motorcyclist position themselves in their lane?

options.text: In the same spot in the lane all the time.
By weaving between different positions to keep other drivers out.
By choosing a position based on road and traffic conditions.
Lane position does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: By choosing a position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are less noticeable.
You are less likely to get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, more alcohol builds up in your body. Never operate a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Can over-the-counter drugs like cold tablets affect your riding ability?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they usually do not affect your riding ability.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, they are safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Understand the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How important are mirror checks?

options.text: They are not important.
They should only be done on long trips.
They should be part of your regular scanning routine.
They are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular scanning. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You can drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is acceptable because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you enter a turn or curve.
